---
title: "Roadmap"
---


Delivered scope from inception to the first staged release, with the tracking issue for each
step. Every item was completed as a tested pull request and verified by execution. The
dates are the issue-close dates. The timeline below is a historical record; it keeps its
filed wording.

## Project timeline

### 3 October — baseline

- The product specification — the implementation plan — is written and reviewed before
  implementation; the board graduates to the GitHub org as issues KA-01…KA-44 with the label,
  effort and milestone catalog, and repository governance follows: branch protection,
  contributing and security policies, Renovate ([KA-21](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/21), [46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/46)–[57](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/57)).
- The engineering standard is committed before any build work: hypothesis-first TDD with
  watched-RED commits, and the OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges in the default row
  ([PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/52), [badges](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/53)).

### 9 October — the two-repo foundation

- The OS repository revives as a real flake — pinned inputs, explicit unfree posture, no global
  CUDA — and the minimal profile evaluates with zero categories enabled, producing a system
  closure ([KA-01](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/1): [skeleton](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/118), [flake](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/122), [closure](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/127)).
- The overlay repository (kailash-packages) seeds as an independently consumable flake — the
  nixpkgs↔NixOS split — and the OS flake.lock pins it at the first lock-time evaluation
  ([KA-02](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/2): [overlay flake](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/5), [pin](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/128)).
- The engineering standard hardens in-repo: harness-before-capability ordering, GitHub Actions
  as the authoritative check surface, and flake-check matrices evaluating both declared systems
  on hosted runners in both repositories ([ordering](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/120), [hosted gates](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/129)).

### 10 October — the taxonomy becomes data

- categories.yaml locks the post-purge census: CORE plus CLASSIC (C-1…C-10), ATTACK (A-1…A-8),
  DEFENCE (D-1…D-7) and OPS (O-1…O-7), with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP-standards mappings carried as
  manifest data ([KA-04](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/4): [CLASSIC census](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/6), [OPS + rename](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/14)).
- tools.yaml defines the entry schema and the manifest validator — unique identifiers, category
  existence, per-layer reconcile counts — committed watched-failing before any tool data lands
  ([KA-05.1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/74), [PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/15)).
- The first bespoke derivations land: garak is pinned commit-exact and smoke-checked against its
  probe index — a hosted-runner packaging defect is caught and fixed the same day — PyRIT is
  packaged, and the kailash CLI opens list / search / info over the manifest ([garak](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/20), [PyRIT](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/16), [CLI](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/17)).
- CI becomes manifest-driven: a committed generator expands the manifest into the build matrix
  in both repositories, and the negative gate — a deliberately broken manifest fails the build
  before any matrix leg runs — is proven ([generator](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/130), [negative gate](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/28)).

### 11 October — manifest complete, gates enforced

- Every surviving tool is entered: CLASSIC 142, ATTACK 58, DEFENCE 46, OPS 91 primary slots —
  337 across 32 census categories, data-packs excluded from counts — and the per-layer totals
  reconcile in the validator ([KA-05](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/5), [CLASSIC entries](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/30)).
- The flagship evaluation stack builds green on hosted runners — garak, PyRIT, promptfoo (its
  freshness decision recorded), ART, counterfit — each acceptance smoke joined to its build leg
  ([KA-10–12](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/10), [acceptance smokes](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/46)).
- Safety becomes mechanical: every tool carrying safety: exp is wrapped by the generator to
  refuse execution outside the double-key lab-mode gate (the host option plus KAILASH_LAB_MODE
  per invocation), and CI fails on wrap or manifest drift ([KA-18/19](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/18), [drift gate](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/149)).
- The hardened profiles — redteam-ai (ATTACK full + O-4) and minimal — evaluate and build
  ([KA-17](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/17), [PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/146)).
- Release engineering is fixed: calendar release trains on 2026.xx with the two-digit release
  index, update cadences by tool-staleness class, the lockfile as the version, and the kailash
  binary cache live ([KA-16](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/16), [KA-47](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/142), [cadence policy](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/guide/releases.md)).

### 12 October — the four layers become modules

- Layer CLASSIC completes C-1…C-10: the exemplar module lands first per the §4.5 contract and
  the siblings generate from it; the Burp-family tools are pinned exact via the lock;
  exploitation remains software-only; the SDR pack is recorded as opt-in data, never on default
  images ([KA-06/07](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/6), [exemplar PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/155)).
- The OPS platform modules land: the MLflow service, k3s/podman compute with ollama and
  llama.cpp, the langchain SDK stack with torch as a Shape-4 pair (non-GPU default, explicit
  -nvidia variant), native and containerised vector stores, local-LLM web UIs, an authoring
  stack, and per-category devShells ([KA-08/09](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/8), [torch shape](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/51)).
- Layer ATTACK opens as category modules: A-1 AI reconnaissance and A-2 prompt injection,
  payload packs as opt-in data, trufflehog cross-listed by the secondary-tags rule
  ([KA-13](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/13), [PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/166)).
- Layer DEFENCE completes D-1…D-7 — guardrails, evals, provenance, threat modelling,
  governance mapping, standards verification — with the packaging-reality gate recording which
  defences ship as derivations ([KA-24](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/24), [PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/177)).
- The VM smoke suite boots the shipped categories inside the distribution and enforces the
  module contract ([suite PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/176)).

### 13 October — 2026.01-alpha.1: the first staged cut

- The ATTACK long tail completes: the agentic/MCP and supply-chain categories (mcp-inspector,
  mcp-scan, guarddog, picklescan, modelscan) and A-5…A-8, with the MLflow-exploit integration
  leg — the pairing thesis executed against the platform's own lab deployment via the real
  MLflow API protocol ([KA-22/23](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/22), [integration leg](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/185);
  the pre-210 tool name rides the [kailash-os#210 registry](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210)).
- O-7 ships agent and MCP operability with short-lived, human-minted capability grants —
  read-class defaults for unsupervised agents ([KA-25](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/25), [PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/182)).
- GVM/OpenVAS arrives as a service module, and the kailash.data.* wordlists and data packs
  flip opt-in with proof legs ([KA-27](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/27), [KA-29](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/29)).
- Platform VM acceptance: a booted platform profile completes an ollama prompt and serves
  MLflow on :5000 ([KA-08.5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/109), [transcript](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/184)).
- The deliverable shape is decided: QEMU images primary, ISOs secondary; the budgets are
  CI-enforced ([KA-28](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/28), [matrix PR](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/181)).
- **The first release publishes**: [2026.01-alpha.1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/releases/tag/2026.01-alpha.1) — the full four-layer catalogue on a
  pinned, reproducible NixOS base, 32 census categories and 337 tool slots; ISO and QEMU
  artefacts attach from hosted runners with artefact-naming and upload-actor checks, and the
  release body carries the gate table: the hosted build (37 legs), flake-check, OpenSSF
  Scorecard, the manifest validator at the pin, and the §11.2 refusal contract — the generator
  refuses the exp-carrying A-8 emit by name ([KA-46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/141), [lock bump](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/196)).
- **Every artefact is born attested**: the release workflow holds an OIDC identity token and
  emits, per artefact and before upload, an in-toto SLSA v1.0 build-provenance statement and an
  SPDX SBOM, signed with a Sigstore certificate and recorded in the public Rekor transparency
  log — verifiable with gh attestation verify ([KA-48 slice](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/198), [attestation listing](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/attestations)).
- The image-matrix completeness amendment builds the four targets the initial cut had not, from
  the tag's pin, and SHA256SUMS covers all twelve matrix artefacts
  ([completeness](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/200), [attach from hosted runners](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/197)).

### 14 October — release engineering completes; the documentation estate opens

- Oversized QEMU images publish in attested chunks with per-leg checksum sheets, keeping SLSA
  attestation intact past GitHub's per-asset cap — and the workflow-trigger defect that would
  otherwise have left four matrix targets never-built is found and fixed ([chunked publishing](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/207), [trigger fix](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/202)).
- The standing release ladder is codified: alpha → rc.1 → GA, the standing cut checklist, and
  per-criterion verdicts at every stage ([KA-49](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/204)).
- The implementation specification is published in-repo, every section citation hyperlinked to
  its anchor — the citation convention all prose surfaces enforce ([KA-51](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/209), [docs/spec.md](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/spec.md)).
- The aarch64 legs of the matrix build natively under the split-arch strategy (hosted x86_64,
  native arm); Raspberry Pi-class support is reported as partial, with the posture decision recorded ([KA-36](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/36)).
- The documentation estate goes live: the [Kailash OS Guide](https://docs.kailash.tools) — the
  taxonomy census, the build's security and governance model, the administrator guide and the
  manifest-generated category directory — and the [Kailash OS Cookbook](https://book.kailash.tools)
  with task-oriented recipes (first image, the garak LLM01 prompt-injection scan,
  attack-then-verify, administrator procedures) ([KA-WS-5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-book/issues/1), [KA-WS-6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-docs/issues/1)).

Work is tracked on the [Kailash Roadmap board](https://github.com/orgs/kailash-os/projects/1)
as issues `KA-NN` across the kailash-os organisation. The OS, the packages overlay, and
the website are separate repositories with a single dependency graph
([the canon map](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/61)). Every issue lands
a runnable artefact with an exit criterion.

## Engineering discipline

Hypothesis-first TDD with watched-RED commits is the engineering standard. The failing
test is written first and committed watched-failing, then made to pass. The RED→GREEN
pair stays visible in every item's history. Harness-before-capability: the check that
would catch a regression ships in the same pull request as the capability it guards.
Each roadmap item decomposes into hour-scale leaf slices. Every commit and tag is
GPG-signed; branch protection verifies at merge. Releases follow the
[cadence policy](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/guide/releases.md):
a train every 6 weeks, alpha → rc.1 → GA, the lockfile as the version. Nothing updates
itself in the background. The loop is
[documented on the Build page](https://kailash.site/build.html).

## Documentation

The specification and its practice are published on three surfaces, generated and verified
against the same pinned manifest revision:

- **kailash.site** — this site: the specification overview (taxonomy, architecture, verification
  standards, governance) and the generated [tools catalogue](https://kailash.site/tools.html).
- **[docs.kailash.tools](https://docs.kailash.tools)** — the Kailash OS Guide, generated from the
  manifest: Part I–IV with the taxonomy census, the build's security and governance model, the
  administrator guide, and the per-category directory
  ([KA-WS-6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-docs/issues/1)); the per-tool
  reference-page generator, with the exemplar reference page live, is the open lane
  ([KA-WS-6.6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-docs/issues/17)).
- **[book.kailash.tools](https://book.kailash.tools)** — the Kailash OS Cookbook: worked, task-
  oriented recipes with real commands and expected output ([KA-WS-5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-book/issues/1)); the recipe
  directory and per-family walkthroughs continue on the book ([book upkeep](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-book/issues/12)).

## Contributing

Contributions follow the [contributing guide](https://kailash.site/contributing.html) and the
[engineering standard](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/AGENTS.md).
Add tools through a manifest entry, never through hand-edited module files. CI validates,
builds, and VM-tests every change. Commits and tags are GPG-signed. Work lands on leaf
branches cut from the default branch. Pick an item from the
[2026.01 completion](https://github.com/orgs/kailash-os/projects/1) or the next train. The
spec section cited in the issue body is the design source. Kailash OS is BSD-3-Clause.
